## $x_1$ seams between blocks (`layout: cubed`, `nb1` > 1) {#sec-ch03-x1seams}

Only the `cubed` layout splits $x_1$ (@sec-ch03-layouts). The vertical schemes of @sec-ch05 are column operations: the
hydrostatic reference is a scan from the top of the column, and several switches read windows that reach past a block
edge. Four mechanisms make a split column match one block. (a) The reference scan is relayed from the top block down,
each block passing its bottom face value to the block below. (b) The reference ghost rows (`pref`, `dref`) are
overwritten with the neighbour's interior rows. (c) Switch-specific ghost rows past the seam are the neighbour's: under `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` the plain-mean
ghost cells and the two face pressures; under the face-flux covariance (on by default) the $x_2$ and $x_3$ face
states one row past the seam, for the hydro and for the scalars; under `SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT` the density
increment one row past it. (d) Across process seams only, the seam-face flux, face pressure
and reference flux are replaced by the mean of the two sides. Wall reconstructions and wall mirroring are gated on a
physical face, so they never act at a seam; column-wide EOS[^rg-b43b7aad09b4] repairs gather the whole column.

Local symbols: $\mathrm{sm}$ (upright) an $x_1$ seam face shared by the block below ($\mathrm{B}$) and above
($\mathrm{T}$); $\mathbf F^{\mathrm{B}}_{\mathrm{sm}}$, $\mathbf F^{\mathrm{T}}_{\mathrm{sm}}$ the $x_1$ fluxes the two blocks compute there;
$p^{\mathrm{top}}$ the reference face pressure a block receives at its upper face; $A_{\mathrm{sm}}$ the area of the seam face
[$\mathrm{m^2}$].

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** A column split into several $x_1$ blocks behaves like one block: the hydrostatic reference scan is
relayed down the column, reference ghost rows are the neighbour's interior rows, switch-specific ghost rows are
exchanged, and across process seams the seam flux is averaged (@eq-ch03-x1seams-average).

**Data.** In/out: reference rows, switch-specific ghost rows and seam fluxes, in their own units.

**Placement.** Each stage: the relay when the well-balanced reconstruction builds its reference; the flux average
on the $x_1$ flux slab, face pressure and `bflux1`, across process seams only.

**Activation.** YAML `distribute: {layout: cubed, nb1}` with `nb1` > 1; default off (`nb1: 1`). Requires
`nghost` $\ge 3$ under `SNAP_WB_REF4`; blocks of one process must run concurrently.

**Guarantee / limits.** Round-off agreement with one block, not bitwise; exact (gap 0) with
`SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT`.

**Evidence.** `test_x1_seam_split` arms, `test_pref_local_seam`, `test_pref_local_seam_flux_covariance`,
`test_parentless_cloud_nb1_mp`; check `[C13]`; the ctest entries were not run for this chapter at the pin (missing evidence).
:::

### Derivation

**Single-valued seam flux.** Let $V_{\mathrm B}$ and $V_{\mathrm T}$ be the volumes of the two cells that share the
seam, the top cell of block B and the bottom cell of block T [$\mathrm{m^3}$]. Block B updates its top cell with
$-A_{\mathrm{sm}}\mathbf F^{\mathrm{B}}_{\mathrm{sm}}/V_{\mathrm B}$ and block T its bottom cell with $+A_{\mathrm{sm}}\mathbf F^{\mathrm{T}}_{\mathrm{sm}}/V_{\mathrm T}$, per
unit time. Multiplying each update by its own volume and by $\Delta t$[^rg-6e5d28d7b425] gives the change of the column total at the
seam per stage:

$$
V_{\mathrm B}\left(-\frac{A_{\mathrm{sm}}\mathbf F^{\mathrm B}_{\mathrm{sm}}}{V_{\mathrm B}}\right)\Delta t
+ V_{\mathrm T}\left(\frac{A_{\mathrm{sm}}\mathbf F^{\mathrm T}_{\mathrm{sm}}}{V_{\mathrm T}}\right)\Delta t
= A_{\mathrm{sm}}\left(\mathbf F^{\mathrm T}_{\mathrm{sm}} - \mathbf F^{\mathrm B}_{\mathrm{sm}}\right)\Delta t ,
$$

zero only if the two agree. Both blocks
replace their value by

$$
\bar{\mathbf F}_{\mathrm{sm}} = \tfrac12\left(\mathbf F^{\mathrm{B}}_{\mathrm{sm}} + \mathbf F^{\mathrm{T}}_{\mathrm{sm}}\right),
$$ {#eq-ch03-x1seams-average}

and floating-point addition is commutative, so both hold the same bits and the sums telescope exactly across the seam.
@eq-ch03-x1seams-average is the seam average in `hydro_forward.cpp`, applied to the flux slab and, packed with it, the
face pressure and the reference flux `bflux1` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}). It is applied only across
process seams; with mechanism (b) the two sides of an in-process seam already compute the same states, and the code
comment states that a same-process seam is not averaged.

**Reference relay.** The default reference is a scan of face pressures down from an anchor at the top of the column,
each cell adding its own hydrostatic drop. Split into blocks, each block needs as anchor the face value the scan has
reached at its upper face. The top block anchors itself; each other block takes $p^{\mathrm{top}}$ from the block above
and, after its own scan, passes its bottom face value down (`take_x1_anchor` and `pass_x1_anchor`,
{{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_hydro_ref_x1 >}}). The relay is serial from top to bottom, so every block's anchor equals the value the
one-block scan has at the same face, up to the order of the additions. The scan kernel itself is in @sec-ch05.

**Ghost rows.** A block's ghost rows of `pref`, `dref` computed locally from its ghost quadrature differ from the
owner's interior values; how far apart near a wall is **not measured at the pin** (the code comment gives a size
without a deck or run). Replacing them by the neighbour's
interior rows, sent under `kWbGhostUpTag` and `kWbGhostDnTag`, makes the perturbation field identical on both
sides of the seam ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_hydro_ref_x1 >}}). Nothing in the derivation is truncated; the remaining differences from one block are round-off from
the order of operations.

The check takes the seam average on $4\times10^5$ random pairs with the two operands in both orders: the
two blocks' results carry identical bit patterns, and the seam's contribution to the column total is exactly zero
at every pair. Without the average the same seam leaves a non-zero residual at every pair, up to
$9.1\times10^3$ in flux units, which is the term @eq-ch03-x1seams-average removes (`[C13]`).[^x1s-c13] The relay
and the ghost rows are covered by the tests below.

[^x1s-c13]: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch03/checks/geometry_check.py`, output `src/snapy_report/ch03/checks/geometry_check.out`,
    line `[C13]`; a numpy port of the $x_1$ seam-face average in `HydroImpl::forward` at the pin, CPU, double; Python 3.11.13, numpy 2.4.6, sympy 1.14.0.

### Numerical method

All four mechanisms run in every stage of a split column. The relay and the ghost-row exchange run inside
`_hydro_ref_x1`, when the well-balanced reconstruction builds its reference; the plain-mean ghost rows before it; the
seam average after the $x_1$ fluxes are computed and before the positivity limiter; the face-pressure ghost rows after
the average. A same-process neighbour is reached through an in-memory board, a remote one through the process group
(@sec-ch14); `_x1_ghost_rows` packs $n_{\mathrm{rows}}$ rows ($n_{\mathrm{rows}}$, its argument `m`, is 1 or $n_g$ = `il` depending on the caller) from below the top face (up) and from above the bottom face (down) and
copies the neighbour's rows into its ghosts. The message tags are 0x7715 (relay), 0x7717 and 0x7718 (reference ghost
rows), 0x7720 and 0x7721 (seam flux), 0x7722 to 0x7725 (face-pressure and plain-mean ghost rows), 0x7726 and 0x7727 (the density increment of the
radial-exact work), 0x7730 to 0x7737 (the covariance face states), and `0x7740 + 4k` to `0x7743 + 4k` for scalar
row $k$[^rg-2dedcdaf1d1e] (the scalar covariance); `_x1_ghost_rows` uses each tag and the next. EOS column repairs
call `gather_x1`, which joins the column's pieces bottom first. @fig-ch03-x1seams-relay shows a column of three blocks.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch03-x1seams-relay
#| fig-cap: "A column split into three $x_1$ blocks. Black arrows: the reference relay, top block to bottom block, one face value per seam. Purple arrows: each block's interior rows copied into the neighbour's ghost rows. At each seam face the two one-sided fluxes (orange) are replaced by their mean when the seam is between processes."
#| fig-alt: "Three stacked blocks with downward arrows at the seams, short arrows into hatched ghost rows, and paired flux arrows at each seam face."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch03.figures.fig_x1seams_relay import make_fig
make_fig()
```

: Code map of the $x_1$ seams. {#tbl-ch03-x1seams-code}

In step order (@tbl-ch03-x1seams-code):

1. Setup refuses `SNAP_WB_REF4` (or `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT`, which implies it) with `nghost` < 3, through
   `wb_ref4_enabled` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}).
2. In the stage, `phys_x1inner` and `phys_x1outer` gate the wall treatments ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}});
   under `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` the plain-mean ghost rows come from the neighbours with `_x1_ghost_rows`
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).
3. `_hydro_ref_x1` takes the anchor from above, scans, passes its bottom face down, and swaps reference ghost rows
   with both neighbours using `kWbGhostDnTag` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_hydro_ref_x1 >}}).
4. After the $x_1$ fluxes, a process seam is averaged with `kSeamFluxDnTag` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}),
   then the face-pressure ghost rows past the seam are exchanged with `_x1_ghost_rows`
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).

**How to use it.** A column split into two blocks held by one process:

```yaml
distribute: {layout: cubed, nb1: 2, blocks_per_process: 2}   # build through Mesh; the blocks run concurrently
```

Refused:

- `nb1` > 1 on another layout ("SlabLayoutImpl: pz must be 1 for slab layout");
- with gravity, `SNAP_WB_REF4` or `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` with `nghost` < 3 ("SNAP_WB_REF4 (or
  SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT, which implies it) needs nghost >= 3, got 2; unset it");
- an implicit scheme ("[Hydro] implicit scheme requires nb1 = 1 (no x1 decomposition): the vertical solve has no
  cross-rank coupling.");
- more than 16 blocks per process when blocks exchange with another process ("[Layout:send_to_block] at most 16 blocks per process").

The seam average @eq-ch03-x1seams-average runs across process seams only
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}):

```cpp
    // No exchange, no behavior change at nb1 = 1. Across process seams only,
    // as with one block per process; a same-process seam is not averaged.
    if (!options->disable_flux_x1() && playout &&
        playout->has_process_group() && playout->options->pz() > 1) {
      auto iloc = playout->loc_of(playout->options->rank());
      int above = playout->neighbor_rank(iloc, {0, 0, 1});
      int below = playout->neighbor_rank(iloc, {0, 0, -1});
      if (above >= 0 && playout->is_local_block(above)) above = -1;
      if (below >= 0 && playout->is_local_block(below)) below = -1;
      if (above >= 0 || below >= 0) {
        constexpr int kSeamFluxUpTag = 0x7720;  // payload travels upward
        constexpr int kSeamFluxDnTag = 0x7721;  // payload travels downward
```

: Tests of the $x_1$ seams. C++ entries carry the build suffix (`.release`). {#tbl-ch03-x1seams-tests}

The reference cases are `local_blocks_restart_the_reference_at_the_seam` ({{< code tests/test_pref_local_seam.cpp HydroRefX1.local_blocks_restart_the_reference_at_the_seam >}}) and
`in_process_split_matches_one_block_after_200_steps` ({{< code tests/test_pref_local_seam.cpp HydroRefX1.in_process_split_matches_one_block_after_200_steps >}}). The arms run one
gtest each with their environment through the CMake function `seam_arm` ({{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}); the
comparisons are in
`split_gap` and its callers ({{< code tests/test_x1_seam_split.cpp split_gap >}}). With `SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT` on, `radial_exact_split_gap`
({{< code tests/test_x1_seam_split.cpp radial_exact_split_gap >}}) requires the split column to equal one block
exactly (gap 0) and its drift of $\mathcal E=\sum_iV_iE_i+P$ (appendix A, notation group 5) to stay within $10^{-13}$; the switch-off control bounds the gap by $10^{-13}$. CUDA twins of four arms (`_x1_centroid_cuda`, `_radial_exact_cuda`, `_radial_exact_off_cuda`, `_wb_ref4_cuda`)
are registered by `seam_arm` when CUDA is built, in the same file; the `_mp` entries run on two ranks with
`torchrun`. They were not run for this chapter at the pin (missing evidence).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- Blocks of one process in a split column must run concurrently; a block waits at most 5 minutes for its anchor.
- At most 16 blocks per process can exchange block messages.
- Under `SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT` a seam cell takes the centred slope of one block through
  `corrected_pe_work_seam` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}), so the corrected-PE work does
  not depend on the $x_1$ decomposition; `test_x1_seam_split_radial_exact` requires a gap of exactly 0 in `radial_exact_split_gap`
  ({{< code tests/test_x1_seam_split.cpp radial_exact_split_gap >}}). A periodic $x_1$ column keeps the one-sided
  slope at its block edges, where `x1_neighbors` returns no neighbour ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}), and setup warns with
  `TORCH_WARN_ONCE` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}). An implicit scheme refuses any $x_1$ split with
  `TORCH_CHECK` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_apply_implicit_correction >}}).
:::

A split column is not bitwise equal to one block; the tests use $10^{-13}$ and $10^{-12}$. How far a split column
differs from one block on CPU and on GPU is **not measured at the pin**. The header comment of
`test_pref_local_seam.cpp` says that `HydroImpl` restarts the scan in a second same-process block and that the test
does not fix it, while the assertions expect the relay of this section ({{< code tests/test_pref_local_seam.cpp >}});
the comment is stale against the code it tests. The switch combinations that are tested are listed in the switch coverage matrix, @sec-ch12-matrix.
